blogdetails.title: How DPS Jankipuram Creates a Positive Learning Environment for Students
blogdetails.description:
A positive learning environment is definitely not in the bricks and mortar. It is about if a child feels free to question, try and not be hesitant about getting it wrong. Learn how DPS Jankipuram builds that kind of space through its teaching and everyday support.

Introduction

Children gleefully running around the campus hints at positivity. But positive learning? It is deeper. It is way more than the echo of laughter during recess or the bright, colorful displays on classroom walls. True positive learning is an internal shift. It is the confidence of a student who knows that mistakes are just data points on the road to understanding. A lively campus shows that children are happy in their environment, positive learning ensures they are flourishing because of it. It happens when curiosity replaces compliance and the pursuit of a grade transforms into the joy of discovery.  DPS Jankipuram is built on that understanding. A child learns best when the environment invites curiosity and feels like they belong there.

As one of the best CBSE schools in Lucknow, we treat the learning environment as something that must be shaped on purpose for the best outcomes.

What a Positive Learning Environment Actually Looks Like at The Best CBSE School in Lucknow

A positive learning environment is one where a student understands. They feel safe enough to take part. At DPS Jankipuram, that means a few things working together:

  • Teaching that rewards questions, not only correct answers

  • Lessons that connect to life outside the classroom

  • Technology used to clarify ideas, not to decorate them

  • Teachers who guide a struggling child instead of moving on

  • Room for students to speak, perform and be heard

The principle underneath all of it is simple. School should not feel like a race that a few children win and the rest lose. It should feel like a place where every child finds something they can do well.

  • School Infrastructure That Earns A Reputation

Good school infrastructure is not measured by how new it looks. It is measured by whether children actually use it. A smart classroom matters only if it changes how a lesson lands. A laboratory matters only if students are inside it, handling equipment, not watching from a bench.

To live up to the trust of being regarded as the best CBSE school in Lucknow, at DPS Jankipuram, we designs our spaces around use, not display:

  • Smart classrooms that turn abstract topics into something students can see and follow

  • Working laboratories and activity areas where children learn by doing

  • A calm, organised campus that lets a child settle and concentrate instead of feeling lost in it

  • Creative spaces for art, music and performance, so talent has somewhere to go

A classroom is four walls until something happens inside it. The infrastructure exists to make sure something does.

  • Experiential Learning, Because Children Remember What They Do

There is a truth most parents have already sensed. A child may forget a definition they read last week but remembers an experiment they ran last month. Experiential learning works because it ties an idea to an action. When they carry it out, the concept becomes something the child has handled.

At DPS Jankipuram, that looks like:

  • Hands-on projects that make a concept stick

  • STEAM activities linking science, technology, engineering, arts and mathematics

  • Early exposure to AI and robotics, so technology feels like something to build with

  • Problem-solving tasks where there is more than one right path

This approach helps every child. It works for those who are not natural memorisers. It changes the question from "Will this come in the exam?" to "How does this work?" 

  • Extracurricular Activities Where Confidence Is Built

For a lot of children, confidence does not start in the classroom. It starts on a field, on a stage, or in a debate they were nervous to enter.

Extracurricular activities are where a child often feels capable at something for the first time. And that feeling rarely stays in one place. A student who learns to hold a stage tends to speak up more in class too.

DPS Jankipuram gives that side of a child room to grow:

  • Sports that build fitness, discipline and the ability to lose and try again

  • Music and performing arts for children who think in colour and sound

  • Debates and quizzes that sharpen how a student speaks and argues

  • House activities and events where teamwork is the point, not the slogan

Some children solve equations fastest. Some score the winning goal. Some hold a room when they speak. A good school makes sure each of them has a stage.

  • Emotional Well-Being That Comes First, Not Last

A child who does not feel safe will not raise their hand. Participation always follows a sense of safety, never the other way around.

This is why emotional support is not something a school bolts on for difficult cases. It is the ground everything else stands on.

DPS Jankipuram builds that ground through:

  • Counselling that any student can reach, not only those in crisis

  • Life-skills sessions that prepare children for situations no exam covers

  • Steady guidance when a child is struggling with something

  • A clear stand against bullying, so school feels safe to be in

  • Activities that teach empathy and patience

When children feel secure, they ask more, share more and stop performing a version of themselves. That is usually the point where real learning starts.

  • Teaching That Meets Each Child Where They Are

One lesson, delivered one way, will reach some children and lose others. Teaching to the middle leaves both ends behind. The strong students drift because they are not stretched. The ones who need a little longer fall quietly behind. Neither shows up clearly in a class average.

DPS Jankipuram works against that with flexible, student-focused teaching:

  • Cooperative learning, where children explain ideas to each other and learn twice

  • Classroom discussion that invites thinking out loud

  • Creative methods for children who learn better by doing than by listening

  • Academic support and individual attention when a child needs it

Finishing the chapter was never the goal. A class that has moved on while half of it is lost has not taught much at all.

Why Parents Choose DPS Jankipuram

Most parents are weighing two things at once. They want a child who is properly prepared for what comes next. They also want that child to have had a childhood worth remembering. Those two goals can pull against each other. A school that only chases results can hollow out the years it is meant to enrich.

Parents choose DPS Jankipuram because it tries to hold both:

  • Solid CBSE academics, taught with care rather than pressure

  • Infrastructure that supports the learning, not just the prospectus

  • Real space for creativity, sport and self-expression

  • A learning environment built around the child, not the average

A child spends a long stretch of important years inside a school. The right environment is what makes those years count for something beyond marks.

Admissions at DPS Jankipuram- The Best CBSE School in Lucknow

Admissions at DPS Jankipuram are less a gate and more an introduction. The aim is to find a genuine fit between what a family wants and what the school does. The process is meant to be clear and unhurried:

  • Helping parents understand how the school actually teaches

  • Sharing honest detail about programmes, facilities and daily life on campus

  • Keeping the admission steps simple and easy to follow

  • Starting the parent-school relationship on a steady footing

For parents looking for the best CBSE school in Lucknow, the admission stage is the natural place to begin. A good beginning shapes the years that follow.

Conclusion

A positive learning environment does not produce children who only score well. It produces children who are willing to think, try and stand up for what they believe. DPS Jankipuram builds that environment by joining a few things that are easy to list and harder to do well: usable infrastructure, teaching that adapts, activities that build confidence and steady emotional support.

As one of the best CBSE schools in Lucknow, at DPS, we work from a plain belief. Education should give a child more than a report card. It should help them find out what they are good at, who they get on with and what they want to do next.

Every child arrives with a different story. A good school simply gives them the room and the reasons to keep writing it.

Your Queries Answered

What makes a positive learning environment at school?

When a school combines interactive teaching, supportive staff, usable facilities and a wide range of activities, it sets forth a positive learning environment. The focus sits on understanding over memorising and on building confidence, communication and emotional steadiness alongside academic results.

What does the school infrastructure at DPS Jankipuram include?

It includes smart classrooms, working laboratories, dedicated activity areas and creative spaces for art and performance. The point of each one is practical: to help students grasp ideas and take part, not simply to look modern.

How do extracurricular activities help students?

They build confidence, teamwork and communication, often in children who do not find that footing in the classroom first. Sports, arts, debates and school events give every student a place to discover what they are good at.

How does DPS Jankipuram support a child's overall development?

Through experiential learning, individual academic guidance, life-skills sessions, accessible counselling and plenty of chances to take part. The aim is to develop both what a child knows and who they are becoming.

Why is DPS Jankipuram considered one of the best CBSE schools in Lucknow?

DPS balances strong CBSE academics with real infrastructure, a full extracurricular programme and a learning environment shaped around the child. That mix supports growth across results, character and confidence.

blogdetails.title: Positive impact on the mindset of children to the rejoining of school
blogdetails.description:
The positive impact of rejoining school extends far beyond academics. It fundamentally transforms children's mindset development through structured social interaction and emotional regulation. This article will help understand the importance of school in your child's holistic growth, this article presents evidence-based insights.

Introduction

Remember when the summer breaks force kitchens to become classrooms and parents turn into substitute teachers? The activities that were practised earlier blurred, and something quietly shifted in our children. They became comfortable being by themselves as screens replaced playgrounds. Emojis substituted for facial expressions. And now, as the schools reopen, many parents quietly wonder: Is my child actually ready to be back? 

The truth is, returning to school does more than restart academics. It reshapes a child’s mindset. Classrooms rebuild routine. Friendships restore confidence. Playground chatter revives social skills that screens simply cannot teach. Rejoining school helps children rediscover structure, curiosity, and the simple joy of learning together.

1. Mental Health Recovery

When children return to school, something powerful happens. Their minds start resetting. Research shows this clearly. A major Harvard study found that mental health diagnoses among children dropped by 43% within nine months of returning to in-person learning. Depression cases alone fell by 60%. Anxiety and ADHD also declined.

Why does this happen?

Because schools offer something psychologists call structured socialisation. Kids learn how to talk. Disagree. Solve problems. Regulate emotions. All in real time. Screens cannot teach that. Studies from Malaysia showed the same pattern. When schools reopened, 72% of primary students and 59% of secondary students reported feeling genuinely happy to be back in classrooms. 

The change is also biological. School routines restore sleep cycles. They reduce endless screen time. They bring back movement, play, and physical activity. All of this supports brain health.
In simple words: School does not just restart studies. It reboots a child’s emotional system.

2. Social-Emotional Learning: The Hidden Curriculum

School brings subjects. But the real lessons? They often happen between classes in the form of Social-Emotional Learning (SEL). It is where children learn how to understand themselves and others. And it mostly happens through everyday interaction.

Here is what children quietly learn in school and how it comes across as a positive impact of rejoining school:

  • Emotional control:- handling frustration during group work or classroom challenges.

  • Empathy:- reading facial expressions, tone, and body language.

  • Conflict resolution:- arguing, negotiating, then becoming friends again.

  • Belonging:- figuring out who they are within a group.

These skills cannot grow in isolation. Schools that actively use SEL programs report fewer behavioural issues and safer environments. When children understand emotions, bullying and aggression tend to fall. At DPS, we understand this hidden truth that school is more than an academic space. It is a training ground for emotional intelligence.

3. Cognitive Growth and Academic Engagement

Learning at home keeps education going. But it has limits. Distractions are everywhere. Feedback is slow. Hands-on learning almost disappears. Classrooms change that. In school, teachers can adjust explanations instantly. Students ask questions in real time. Group discussions spark curiosity. Experiments bring concepts alive.

Peer learning also plays a big role. When children explain ideas to each other, understanding becomes deeper. Research from Shanghai found that students who focused on learning rather than just grades adjusted better after returning to school. Supportive classrooms helped reduce academic stress.

4. Routine, Structure, and Psychological Safety

Children thrive on routine. Wake up. Go to school. Attend classes. Play with friends. Return home. This simple structure has a powerful impact. During long breaks or disruptions, this rhythm disappears. Sleep cycles shift. Study habits weaken. Days feel unstructured. School brings order back.

The positive impact of rejoining school includes:

  • Fixed schedules that regulate sleep and energy

  • Clear spaces for learning and relaxation

  • Defined roles – they are students again, not just kids at home

  • Gradual challenges that build confidence step by step

Research from Finland found that while mental health concerns rose during pandemic disruptions, feelings of loneliness dropped significantly once students returned to school. It is worth understanding that connection matters. Routine creates stability. Stability creates confidence.

5. Physical Health and Child Mindset Development

School is not just about classrooms. It is also about playgrounds. Everything matters when it comes to the positive impact of rejoining school: 

  • Running during recess. 

  • Playing sports. 

  • Walking between classes. 

  • Even standing during activities.

Schools naturally encourage movement. They reduce excessive screen time. They create opportunities for outdoor exposure and sunlight. These small daily habits build long-term health. In an era when children are turning into couch potatoes, when childhood obesity and screen dependency are rising, school environments act as protective systems for physical well-being.

6. Resilience Building and Future Readiness

Returning to school is not always easy, especially after long breaks. Some children feel nervous at first. But this transition itself builds resilience. Children relearn how to adapt. How to face challenges. How to navigate friendships and academic pressure.

Studies from the Netherlands show that children with strong school support systems recover from stress faster than those without them. Schools act as recovery environments. They teach children to:

  • handle stress

  • develop a growth mindset

  • set goals for the future

  • believe in their abilities

These lessons last far beyond the classroom. Because in the end, school does not just prepare children for exams. It prepares them for life.

Conclusion

The evidence is unequivocal: the positive impact of rejoining school on child mindset development is significant and multifaceted. For parents, understanding the importance of school helps contextualise adjustment challenges. Some children will transition seamlessly; others will need support navigating social anxiety or academic gaps. Both responses are normal. What matters is consistent attendance, open communication with teachers, and patience with the process. 

At DPS Jankipuram, we nail it all. Our planned back-to-school sessions give children a warm welcome and double their energy + love for learning!

Your Queries Answered

1. What are the warning signs that my child is struggling with school reintegration?

Ans - Frequent stomachaches before school, sudden clinginess, avoiding friends, or falling grades are some signs. The constant “I don’t want to go” is also a sign. A little hesitation is normal. But if these signs stay for a month or more, it’s time to speak with teachers or a counsellor.

2. What are the school benefits for kids on emotional development compared to online learning?

Ans - School is a live lab for emotions. Kids learn teamwork, conflict resolution, confidence, and friendships in real time. Teachers guide them. Peers challenge them. Routines ground them. Screens teach lessons. Schools teach life.

3. What can parents do to support their child's mindset development during school transitions?

Ans - Keep routines steady. Avoid letting anxiety win over attendance. Talk to teachers often. Encourage sports or clubs. And most importantly stay calm yourself. Kids borrow their emotional cues from parents. When you’re steady, they adjust faster.

4. How long does it usually take children to readjust after returning to school?

Ans - Most children settle back within 2–4 weeks. New routines, friends, and classroom rhythms slowly feel normal again. Some kids adjust faster, others need a little more time. Patience, encouragement, and consistent school attendance help speed up the process.

5. Can extracurricular activities help children readjust to school life?

Ans - Absolutely. Sports, arts, music, or clubs help children reconnect with peers in a relaxed setting. They build confidence, reduce stress, and make school feel enjoyable again. Often, friendships formed outside the classroom make the transition back to school smoother.

Introduction

Nobody remembers the chapter on photosynthesis at their school reunion. They remember the MUN conference where they argued for a position they did not personally believe in and somehow won. The basketball final that went to the last second. The theatre production where everything went slightly wrong and the audience loved it anyway. School is twelve years of a child's life. What happens in those twelve years shapes who they become. And increasingly, parents searching for CBSE schools in Lucknow are understanding this, looking for schools that shape personalities through a range of activities. 

What Makes an Extracurricular Program in CBSE Schools in Lucknow Truly Good?

A long activity list means nothing if students rarely participate. Good extracurricular programs usually have three things:

  • Consistent student involvement

  • Professional guidance and infrastructure

  • Opportunities beyond the school campus

The top schools in Lucknow understand this well. They create spaces where students can explore interests early and develop them seriously over time. One child may discover confidence through theatre. Another may become disciplined through sports. Someone else may find their voice in debate or MUN. That variety matters.

The Shift Parents Are Noticing in CBSE Education

Earlier, extracurriculars were treated like “extra”. Academics came first and everything else came later. That mindset is changing quickly. Today, colleges and future workplaces both look for students who can collaborate, communicate, lead and think independently. Activities outside textbooks help build exactly those qualities. This is why, while parents are Googling, “ CBSE school near me” they search for answers to deeper questions:

  • Does the school have clubs?

  • Are sports taken seriously?

  • Do students participate in competitions?

  • Is there exposure beyond academics?

These questions are important because extracurricular learning shapes personality in ways classrooms alone cannot.

Top Schools in Lucknow that Offer Holistic Education

A perfect combo of academics and extracurricular activities is what serves holistic education best. Here’s a list of schools that have mastered the role: 

1. DPS Jankipuram

DPS Jankipuram Extension has been around long enough to know what actually builds a child beyond the classroom. The school runs structured clubs across middle and senior grades. Not the kind that meet once a term. The kind that gives students something to work toward every week.

Jaipuria Lucknow is the only Microsoft Certified and Microsoft Showcase School in Lucknow, recognised for three consecutive years. Students participate in things that actually mean something outside the school gates.

Extracurricular activities:

  • Sports delivered with a structured, subject-like syllabus - swimming, shooting, taekwondo, yoga, basketball and table tennis

  • MUN participation at national and international virtual conferences, with students receiving High Commendation

  • Coding, gamification and digital tools including Minecraft, Sway and Prezi integrated into student life

3. GD Goenka Public School, Lucknow

GD Goenka ranked first in Lucknow in the C-Fore School Rankings for 2024. The school has earned that position consistently and the extracurricular programme is a big part of why. It is not a long list of activities that exist on paper. It is a working ecosystem where students from different grades regularly participate, compete and develop real capability.

  • Gymnastics, theatre, yoga, aerobics, taekwondo and robotics running alongside the sports programme

DPS Eldeco has been running since 2000. That is a long time to build something. The sports culture here is one of the strongest in the city. The school has eleven FIDE-rated chess players. That one fact tells you more about the seriousness of their sports programme than a paragraph of description would. Beyond sports, the school runs its own MUN conference, which is a marker of genuine co-curricular ambition.

  • DPSEMUN, the school's own Model United Nations conference

  • Structured clubs and societies across school grades with consistent weekly engagement

5. Amity International School, Viraj Khand

Amity Viraj Khand runs across a 3.4-acre campus and offers both day and boarding options. The school hosted the Regional CBSE Science Exhibition, which is the kind of thing that only happens when a school has earned that level of trust. The extracurricular offering here goes noticeably beyond the standard. The Rocksport adventure camp alone is something most Lucknow schools do not offer.

Extracurricular activities:

  • MUN at Oxford MUN level, inter-school football tournament (Strikethon), karate with students winning gold at competitions, yoga and SDG-linked sustainability projects

  • Rocksport outdoor adventure camp developing resilience and teamwork beyond the campus

  • Elected Student Council giving students genuine leadership responsibility

What Parents Should Actually Look For During School Visits

If you are exploring a CBSE school near me, do not stop at brochures. Ask practical questions instead:

  • How often are club activities conducted?

  • Do students participate in competitions outside school?

  • Are activities optional or actively encouraged?

  • Is there dedicated faculty support?

  • Are students across classes involved or only a selected few?

You can usually tell within one campus visit whether extracurricular culture is active or only promotional.

Conclusion

Students rarely remember only classroom lectures years later. They remember debate victories, theatre rehearsals, basketball matches, school concerts, community drives and whatnot. They offered fun while shaping their skills and personalities. That is exactly why extracurricular programs have become such an important factor for parents evaluating CBSE schools in Lucknow today.

The schools making the biggest impact are the ones creating balanced learners. Review the list of top CBSE schools in Lucknow. Schedule a visit and make a decision that best serves your child’s future.

Do extracurricular activities help in college admissions?

Ans - Yes. Participation in sports, debates, MUNs, theatre, music and community programs strengthens student profiles and showcases leadership, consistency and skill development beyond academics.

How can parents evaluate extracurricular culture in a school?

There are fees ranging from ₹7,000 to ₹25,000+ monthly. To top it all, you have your mind racing when it thinks that your child's school shapes not just academic outcomes but social-emotional development. It plays an important role in their values and future opportunities. So, how do you distinguish genuine excellence from marketing gloss? Understand the evaluation criteria. Here we will distill what separates the best schools in Lucknow from the merely adequate and what are features that you must watch out for.

  • 3-year CBSE results – Distinction rates above 60% are a healthy sign

  • Competitive exam pipeline – IIT-JEE, NEET, CLAT, CUET success rates

  • University placements – Where do students go after Class 12?

5. Value-Based Education Matters

Children spend a large part of their day at school. So the values they learn there matter deeply. The best schools focus on character building alongside academics. Look for schools that provide:

One small observation helps parents here: Watch how teachers speak to students during your visit. Respectful communication says a lot about school culture.

A smooth admission experience usually reflects good school administration.

8. Safety Is Non-Negotiable at the Best Schools in Lucknow

Parents today rightly prioritise safety. The best schools in Lucknow treat safety as core infrastructure. Essential safety systems include:

  • Staff background verification

  • CCTV surveillance across campus

9. Strong Parent-School Partnerships

Education works best when schools and parents work together. Top schools encourage regular communication. Good partnership systems include:

  • Mobile apps with student progress updates

  • Parenting workshops and seminars

  • Parent volunteering opportunities

10. Fees and Value Transparency
